name: Singapore

facts.religion: Buddhist about 31%, Christian about 19%, Muslim about 16%, Taoist and Hindu

snapshot: Singapore's government warned that Asia was "particularly exposed" as oil prices jumped more than 60 percent during the Iran war, rattling a city that runs on trade.
culture: Singapore's Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian communities live together under policies that mix public housing blocks by ethnicity. Hawker centres, where cheap stalls sell chicken rice and laksa, are on UNESCO's heritage list. Singlish, a creole of English, Malay, Hokkien and Tamil, is a beloved if officially discouraged badge of identity.
society: Singapore is one of the world's richest places per head and a major port, refining and finance centre. More than 80 percent of residents live in government-built flats. The People's Action Party has ruled since 1959. Laws on public order and speech are strict, and the death penalty is used for drug trafficking.
situation: Singapore has no oil, no gas and barely any land, yet it is one of the world's great refining and shipping hubs. That makes it a sensitive gauge of a war thousands of miles away. When Iran choked shipping through the Strait of Hormuz in 2026, Singapore felt it fast.

On 2 April, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong gave a video address telling Singaporeans that oil prices had risen more than 60 percent since the war began, that Asia was "particularly exposed" because so much Gulf energy flows to it, and that no country, "least of all a small island-nation like ours," could be insulated (Prime Minister's Office). Refineries cut output and sourced crude elsewhere; Australia now supplies over a third of Singapore's LNG; a ministerial crisis committee coordinated the home front, and the government brought forward help for households and businesses. The surprise was resilience. Singapore's economy grew 6 percent in the first quarter, driven by demand for AI chips, though Wong warned in June that slower growth and higher inflation were still coming (AFP via Malay Mail). A year after he won his first election warning of "storm clouds," the storm arrived, and his People's Action Party, in power since 1959, is being judged on how it weathers it.
power: A parliamentary republic in the Westminster model. The prime minister leads the majority in Parliament, elected largely through multi-member constituencies that favour the PAP; the elected president has custodial powers over reserves and key appointments.
holders: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong (PAP), in office since 2024.
